reason: E2 shows that 1 at% Gd microalloying in Pd–Ni–P significantly impacts glass-forming ability due to its different atomic properties, supporting the size-mismatch and nucleation-retardation premises. However, E1 discusses P additions in Ni-based alloys without mentioning Gd or rare-earth microalloying, so it does not support the claimed analogy to Ni–P systems. The premise about shifting crystallization to higher temperatures is not directly evidenced in the cited passages.
premises: Gd microalloying increases atomic size mismatch and disrupts local ordering in metallic glasses
Gd microalloying raises liquid viscosity and retards nucleation kinetics during solidification
Gd microalloying shifts crystallization to higher temperatures upon reheating
The mechanism is analogous to prior observations in Ni–P and Pd–Ni–P systems
The beneficial effect is expected at low microalloying levels (~1 at%)
